post.title: He's Late, So He's Unreliable? #shorts
post.description: Dev is 20 minutes late and Milo decides he's just unreliable. A week later Milo is late himself, and it's the bus. In a classic 1967 study (Edward Jones & Victor Harris, Journal of Experimental Social Psychology), Duke students read an essay for or against Fidel Castro and guessed the writer's real attitude. Even when told a debate coach had assigned the side, readers still judged the pro-Castro writer as far more pro-Castro than the anti-Castro writer (the gap was bigger when the writer chose freely). Lee Ross later (1977) called this tendency to blame the person and overlook the situation the fundamental attribution error. The Milo-is-late-too beat is a story, not part of the study. #psychology #shorts #mindset
